To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we have developed a new approach to predict the spread of information on social networks that does not rely on a diffusion structure, that can be applied to any kind of information, that is fast to run, and that has a good predictive performance.
we introduce a novel method for learning social network embeddings for information diffusion prediction that outperforms state of the art approaches.
we propose a new model for predicting the diffusion process in social networks that is based on the idea of learning the diffusion kernel from the observed cascades.

the following question: Given the temporal dynamics of a social media diffusion process, can we learn a mapping of nodes to a continuous space such that information diffusion can efficiently be modeled as a diffusion process in this latent space?

the proposed method outperforms all the baselines in terms of prediction accuracy and is the fastest in terms of inference time.

our method provides an efficient and scalable approach for learning a continuous diffusion model from cascade samples, which is able to capture complex dynamics and predict the spread of a given piece of information in the social network.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we propose a new method for learning a diffusion kernel from observed diffusion cascades.
our method can be used for predicting information diffusion on social media by leveraging the temporal information of cascades and the interactions between the nodes.
we propose to learn a latent space where information diffusion is a heat diffusion process, and we propose to use a variational auto-encoder to learn this latent space.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the proposed approach can be used to learn a diffusion kernel from observed diffusion cascades without requiring any prior information about the diffusion process and that the learned kernel can be used to predict the spread of new pieces of information with high accuracy and in a very efficient way.
learning a latent space representation for information diffusion can lead to a better modeling of the underlying process and can provide a more efficient solution to the prediction task.
the diffusion of information on the Web can be modeled as a heat diffusion process on an embedding space that can be learned from the data.
